title: Programming Languages
tagline: Syntax and semantics, the lambda calculus, interpreters, scope and binding, type systems, type inference, polymorphism, control and concurrency
summary: Programming languages are designed artefacts with precise meanings, and understanding their principles makes every language easier to learn and use well. This course studies syntax and semantics, the lambda calculus, writing interpreters, names, scope and binding, type systems and type inference, polymorphism, subtyping and modules, and control constructs from exceptions and continuations to concurrency.

chapters.title: Syntax and semantics
chapters.summary: Abstract syntax, grammars for programs, and operational and denotational semantics.

chapters.title: The lambda calculus
chapters.summary: Abstraction and application, reduction, Church encodings and evaluation strategies.

chapters.title: Interpreters
chapters.summary: Writing an evaluator for a small language, with environments and closures.

chapters.title: Names, scope and binding
chapters.summary: Static and dynamic scope, binding times, parameter-passing mechanisms and the lifetime of storage.

chapters.title: Type systems
chapters.summary: Typing rules, type safety through progress and preservation, and the simply typed lambda calculus.

chapters.title: Type inference
chapters.summary: Constraint generation, unification and Hindley–Milner type inference.

chapters.title: Polymorphism, subtyping and modules
chapters.summary: Parametric polymorphism, subtyping, objects and module systems.

chapters.title: Exceptions and continuations
chapters.summary: Exceptions, continuations, generators and coroutines as control constructs.

chapters.title: Concurrency in programming languages
chapters.summary: Shared memory and message passing, actors, futures and async–await.
